- Black-swan/moderate macro shock (15–20% probability): A macro slowdown or ad-market contraction triggers broad tech sell-off. AMZN, though diversified, is not immune — price drops accelerate to the 200‑SMA or below before stabilization.

- Small tactical short: Enter if price fails to reclaim the 10‑EMA (151.749) within 1–2 sessions AND macdh widens negative with rising volume. Entry trigger: daily close below ~148 with volume ≥ recent average (47.34M baseline). Stop: 1.5 ATR above entry. Target: first support ~143.3, with trailing to 138 if momentum persists.
- Put spread (options): Buy put spreads with strike near-the-money and sell lower strikes around 140–135 to limit premium. This plays a downside move while capping cost, recognizing the structural long-term bias that makes outright shorts risky.
- Avoid large short positions because long-term trend still provides tail risk against bears; size conservatively.

Watch-list triggers that would invalidate the bearish case
- A convincing daily close > 10‑EMA (151.749) accompanied by improving MACD histogram and volume above average would remove the immediate momentum-based basis for the short and suggest bulls regained control.
- Conversely, any daily close below 143.3 on above-average sell volume would materially strengthen the bear case and justify increasing exposure to downside strategies.

Final take — what the bull is overlooking
- The bull narrative relies on buyers showing up at predictable technical levels and on AWS/ads growth continuing to outpace market concerns. That’s an optimistic sequence of events requiring disciplined buying behavior and no macro shocks.
- The technicals show a fragile short-term setup: negative MACD histogram, price under the 10‑EMA, neutral RSI, narrow ATR buffer to support.
